answer: A voyage across an agent economy should pass through a karst of checkpoints, not open water. Before an agent can earn, it locks a refundable stake and a verifiable work history into a single identity record; each completed job adds a checkpoint, like water cutting a channel through limestone. A sybil farm must fund and age every fake identity separately, and any fraud forfeits the stake and poisons the whole river of linked identities, so the cost of faking a hundred agents dwarfs the profit of one.
